primitives.note: Five bolts fired over 0.25s are separately timed damage instances against the same target, with a per-subsequent-bolt bonus and (per wiki notes) the total split evenly among however many bolts connect.
Vision of Empire deals its damage in one instance on a fixed 1.5s delay after cast, on cooldown.

Nevermove only deals damage/roots if the wave reaches max range and homes back to detonate on the first enemy hit; against a stationary dummy this requires assuming Swain casts it at max range so the return-and-detonate condition is met.

Nevermove has a recast (the pull) available while the target is rooted; the recast itself deals no damage but collects a Soul Fragment (heal/stat), so it is a separately timed follow-up part of the ability.
Demonic Ascension is a stance with its own drain damage/heal that ends and reverts, distinct from the base kit, and unlocks the separate Demonflare active while active.
While in Demonic Ascension, Swain deals magic damage and heals every 0.5s per enemy target drained.

Demonic Ascension is maintained by a Demonic Energy meter (starts at 50, decays 5/tick then 7.5/tick after 5s, regenerates 10/tick while draining a champion) that gates how long the stance and its DoT/heal persist.
Mana costs (40-60 Q, 60-80 W, 50-70 E, 100 R) may meaningfully limit how many casts fit in a 15s fight.

needsBespoke.why: Two mechanics resist the closed primitive list's flat modeling. (1) Q's five bolts: the bin computes each bolt's damage from an escalating 25%-bonus-per-subsequent-hit formula (InitialDamage, ExtraBoltDamage, MaxDamage), while the wiki notes instead describe the ability's total damage as being split evenly across however many bolts land on a single target -- these are two different damage models for the same ability and a script needs a explicit chosen formula, not just a per-hit damage value. (2) R's Demonic Ascension is a resource-driven stance: its duration is governed by a Demonic Energy meter that decays at a rate which itself changes after 5s, but regenerates while draining any enemy champion (a dummy counts as one) and fully refills on a takedown; whether this makes the stance self-sustaining for the whole fight, when/how often Demonflare can be recast during it (a cooldown value exists in the bin but is flagged as tooltip-only by the wiki), and the automatic cast on expiry all require bespoke state-machine logic beyond a fixed cooldown/duration/DoT primitive.

unsettled.question: Does Death's Hand's total damage get split evenly among the bolts that connect with a single target, or does each bolt deal its own bin-calculated amount (base+AP for the first, +25% bonus per subsequent hit, uncapped by an even split)?
options: Use the bin's per-bolt formulas directly: bolt 1 = InitialDamage, bolts 2-5 each = InitialDamage*1.25 (or similarly escalating), summing above the tooltip's 'total damage' figure
Follow the wiki note: compute the tooltip 'total damage' for however many bolts hit, then divide evenly across those bolts, so 5/5 bolts hitting yields 5 equal instances summing to MaxDamage
quotes: The total damage to a single target will be split evenly among each bolt that hits, meaning that hitting with more bolts will deal less damage per hit (but more overall damage).

unsettled.question: Against a single stationary target that counts as an enemy champion, does draining it during Demonic Ascension generate enough Demonic Energy (10/tick) to outpace or match the decay (5/tick, then 7.5/tick after 5s), letting the stance (and its DoT/heal) persist for the whole 15s fight rather than expiring quickly?
options: Energy regen from draining the dummy keeps net energy flat or rising (capped at 50), so Ascension is effectively permanent once cast on a single target dummy fight
Decay and regen are not simultaneous/additive as assumed, or some other rule caps effective drain time, so Ascension still expires within a few seconds despite continuous draining
quotes: '''Swain''' generates {{as|10 Demonic Energy|azakana}} every {{fd|0.5}} seconds while draining from at least one enemy {{tip|champion}}
decays by {{as|5|azakana}} every {{fd|0.5}} seconds, increased to {{as|{{fd|7.5}}|azakana}} after 5 seconds have elapsed

unsettled.question: Can Demonflare be manually recast repeatedly during Demonic Ascension on some cooldown (the bin lists DemonflareCooldownTooltip=8 but the R part's authors flagged it as tooltip-only/unused), or does it only fire once automatically when Ascension expires (up to the 100-cast lifetime cap)?
options: Demonflare has a real ~8s per-cast cooldown and can be cast manually multiple times per Ascension activation, in addition to the automatic cast on expiry
Demonflare is only cast automatically once, when Demonic Ascension ends (if it isn't on cooldown at that moment), and cannot otherwise be freely recast mid-stance
quotes: does so automatically when ''Demonic Ascension'' expires if ''{{ai|Demonflare|Swain}}'' is not on cooldown at the time of expiration

proposal: Open with Nevermove (E) cast at maximum range so the wave homes back and detonates on the dummy immediately, dealing its magic damage.
Follow with Death's Hand (Q) cast at point-blank range/facing the dummy so all five bolts connect for maximum total damage.
Cast Vision of Empire (W) targeted on the dummy; it explodes 1.5s after cast for magic damage.
Cast Demonic Ascension (R) to enter the drain stance, dealing repeating tick damage (and self-healing, irrelevant to damage dealt) every 0.5s while channeling on the dummy.
While in Demonic Ascension, cast Demonflare whenever it becomes available (assumed ~8s cadence) for its burst nova damage, layered on top of the drain ticks.
Recast Q and E on cooldown throughout the remaining fight duration, weaving them between R's drain ticks and Demonflare casts.
Recast W again if its cooldown (18-22s) comes up before the 15s fight ends (unlikely at rank 1-2, more likely at higher ranks/haste).
If mana becomes limiting, prioritize Q (cheapest, shortest cooldown) and R/Demonflare (largest single hits) over W.
questions: Is it correct to assume Swain can always position at Nevermove's exact max range against a stationary dummy, or should a shorter-range cast (no return/detonate, no damage) be modeled as the default/likely case?

Does entering Demonic Ascension on a single-target dummy fight effectively become a permanent stance for the whole 15s (per the energy-regen question above), meaning R is only cast once, or does it need to be recast on cooldown after expiring partway through the fight?
How often can Demonflare actually be cast per Ascension activation, and should the rotation model it as a fixed-cadence DoT/burst hybrid or as a single guaranteed cast at stance end?

Should Nevermove's recast (pull) be included in the rotation for its heal-adjacent Soul Fragment collection even though it deals no damage itself, or omitted entirely since the damage fight only cares about damage output?
Given Q/W/E/R costs, is mana actually a binding constraint in a 15s fight at the levels/items being simulated, or is it safe to assume unlimited-effective mana for the rotation?
